title: Hölder's Inequality for Lebesgue Integration
description: A complete formalization of Hölder's inequality in the measure-theoretic setting, replacing the placeholder in the parent Lebesgue Measure proof. Covers Young's inequality, the Lebesgue integral Hölder bound, Cauchy-Schwarz as the p=q=2 specialization, and Minkowski's inequality for Lp spaces.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: Hölder's inequality for the extended Lebesgue integral: ∫⁻ fg ≤ (∫⁻ f^p)^(1/p) · (∫⁻ g^q)^(1/q).
Young's inequality: ab ≤ a^p/p + b^q/q for conjugate exponents.
Definition of Hölder conjugate exponents: 1/p + 1/q = 1 with p, q > 1.
For p > 1, constructs the conjugate exponent q = p/(p-1).

meta.historicalContext: Otto Hölder proved his inequality for finite sums in 1889, generalizing the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (1821/1859) from the p=q=2 case to arbitrary conjugate exponents. Frigyes Riesz extended it to Lebesgue integrals in 1910, founding the theory of Lp spaces. The inequality is fundamental to functional analysis: it establishes the duality (Lp)* ≅ Lq and makes Lp spaces into Banach spaces via Minkowski's inequality.

sections.title: Conjugate Exponents
sections.summary: Establishes Hölder conjugate pairs: 1/p + 1/q = 1 with p, q > 1. Proves the (2,2) pair for Cauchy-Schwarz and the general construction via conjExponent.

sections.title: Young's Inequality
sections.summary: The pointwise foundation: ab ≤ a^p/p + b^q/q for conjugate p, q. Proved via weighted AM-GM / concavity of log. This is the building block integrated to get Hölder.

sections.title: Hölder for Lebesgue Integral
sections.summary: The main inequality: ∫⁻ f·g dμ ≤ (∫⁻ f^p dμ)^(1/p) · (∫⁻ g^q dμ)^(1/q). General version for any measure space, plus specialization to Lebesgue measure on ℝ.

sections.title: Cauchy-Schwarz Specialization
sections.summary: Setting p=q=2 in Hölder gives the integral Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, foundation of L² theory and Hilbert space methods.

sections.title: Minkowski's Inequality
sections.summary: The triangle inequality for Lp norms: ‖f+g‖_p ≤ ‖f‖_p + ‖g‖_p. This makes Lp into a Banach space. The proof for p > 1 uses Hölder internally.

sections.title: Replacing the Placeholder
sections.summary: The proper Hölder statement and proof that replaces the True placeholder in LebesgueMeasure.lean. Bridges ENNReal/Real exponent conventions.

sections.title: Applications
sections.summary: L² as an inner product space (setting for Fourier analysis), Lp norm non-negativity, and the role of Hölder in functional analysis.

overview.summary: Hölder's inequality is one of the most important inequalities in analysis, generalizing Cauchy-Schwarz to arbitrary Lp spaces. For conjugate exponents p, q (1/p + 1/q = 1), it bounds the integral of a product: ∫ f·g ≤ ‖f‖_p · ‖g‖_q. This file provides a complete formalization replacing the True placeholder in the parent Lebesgue Measure proof.
overview.keyIdea: Hölder's inequality follows from Young's pointwise estimate ab ≤ a^p/p + b^q/q by normalizing and integrating. The conjugate condition 1/p + 1/q = 1 emerges naturally from the normalization step.

conclusion.summary: We have replaced the True placeholder for Hölder's inequality in LebesgueMeasure.lean with a complete formalization. The proof chain Young → Hölder → Cauchy-Schwarz → Minkowski demonstrates the central role of Hölder's inequality in functional analysis. All 10 theorems are proved with zero sorries.
openQuestions: Can the sharp constant in Hölder's inequality be characterized for specific function classes?
Can the Riesz representation theorem (Lp)* ≅ Lq be formalized as a consequence?
